EMU128_X86_64 SumWideningSpanU32 the port has fewer instructions but more branches (6 against 4, 11 against 8 and 8 against 6): LLVM unrolls the port's much smaller kernel loop (two 16-byte iterations per pass for LargestDigit, four 4-byte iterations per pass for SumWidening) behind a prologue that peels the odd iterations (testb $0x10 or $0xc, jne or je)

EMU128_X86_64 UTF8LookupSpanU8 the port's table lookups are unrolled per byte (andl of the index, a movzbl load from a stack copy of the table, movd) and merged with SIMD unpacks (punpcklbw, punpcklwd, punpckldq), and the rest of the kernel works on whole vectors (movdqa, pand, psubusb, psrlw, por, pxor); highway's EMU128 version moves the lanes through general-purpose registers and shifts them into place at every step (movq, orq, movl, shlq, shrq, shll, andq)
EMU128_X86_64 UTF8LookupStepU8 the port's table lookups are unrolled per byte (andl of the index, a movzbl load from a stack copy of the table, movd) and merged with SIMD unpacks (punpcklbw, punpcklwd, punpckldq), and the rest of the kernel works on whole vectors (movdqa, pand, psubusb, psrlw, por, pxor); highway's EMU128 version moves the lanes through general-purpose registers and shifts them into place at every step (movq, orq, movl, shlq, shrq, shll, andq)
EMU128_X86_64 ZeroingSelectedF32 the port is the one SSE2 instruction of the operation (plus a movdqa or a constant operand); highway's EMU128 additionally splits, masks or merges the vector in pieces (pshufd, punpckldq, punpcklwd, punpcklqdq, pand, por or orps with constant masks, paddq, psllq, orq, movzbl, shll)
